messages:
anna-support: Hey team — just got escalated from @jess (customer-jess). Their hosted inference calls to /v1/generate in eu-west-1 are intermittently returning 502/504 gateway errors for the last 45m. Customer sees TLS handshake timeouts in their client logs. Request IDs: rQw7-3f2, rQw7-3f3, rQw7-3f8. They say it started right after a cert rotation window we ran 37m ago. Can SRE/Runtime triage?

sam-sre: Thanks — grabbing logs. Do we have ingress LB and edge cert rotation events correlating? I see a cert rotation job at +32m from our deploy bot. ci-bot: deploy/cert-rotation job succeeded (job-id: cert-rot-2026-03-14-2132) :white_check_mark:

devon-runtime: On it. Early hypothesis: some resolvers still returning old A records or intermediate cert chain not fully propagated to certain CDN PoPs, causing handshake retries/timeouts and our gateway to return 502s when connection pool exhausted. Any customer repro info?

anna-support: Customer supplied a short curl trace and browser stack: "curl: (35) SSL connect error: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure" and their app logs show ENAHANDSHAKE for 2–10% of requests. They also ran `dig +trace` and got stale A records from their ISP resolver for one of our edge IPs.

maria-ops: I pulled edge logs for eu-west-1: around the window we have spikes of TLS handshake timeouts (SYN succeeded, TLS handshake hung until backend gave up). Also some `alert_unknown_ca` on the freshest certificate when parsed by certain client TLS stacks — suggests cert chain incomplete (missing intermediate). But our cert-rot job uploaded the chain in the normal bundle.

rohit-platform: Could be two simultaneous issues: (1) our cert chain packaging omitted the intermediate for a subset of hosts by mistake (config mismatch during rotation), (2) stale DNS from resolvers causing traffic to reach an older edge pool with a cached incomplete chain. I will diff the bundles.

devon-runtime: Sharing quick repro steps for SRE to reproduce from inside our network:
```
# from a eu-west-1 jumpbox
curl -v --resolve example-infer.redwood.test:443:52.17.123.45 https://example-infer.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' --max-time 10
openssl s_client -connect example-infer.redwood.test:443 -servername example-infer.redwood.test -showcerts
# also test direct to edge IP
openssl s_client -connect 52.17.123.45:443 -showcerts
```

sam-sre: Running the openssl connect to the public IP reproduces a truncated chain: server sends leaf only, not the intermediate. When the client attempts to verify, older resolvers with cached A records route to nodes that still have the previous (now-misconfigured) cert bundle. That explains the intermittent nature. I'm seeing a config template applied to hostgroup eu-edge-03 that omitted the intermediate cert file due to a variable name typo in the rotation script.

rohit-platform: Confirmed. The rotation job used `--cert-bundle $BUNDLE` but for eu-edge-03 $BUNDLE was empty because of a missing env export during the parallel job run. The rest of the fleet got the correct bundle. Opening rollback/patch.

maria-ops: Mitigation options: 1) re-run cert rotation for eu-edge-03 with corrected bundle (fast), 2) temporarily route traffic away from eu-edge-03 using smart-routing (fallthrough to eu-edge-01/02), 3) raise TTL advisory to partners to flush caches (not controllable). Recommend 1+2 to minimize customer impact.

devon-runtime: Can we do a localized rerun without global orchestration? Need to avoid triggering another rolling rotation across fleet.

rohit-platform: Yes — re-run cert install job with `node-target=eu-edge-03 --single` and ensure `BUNDLE` env is set. I'll push the patch and kick the job now. ci-bot: deploy/cert-rot-eu-edge-03 job started (job-id: cert-rot-eu03-2026-03-14-2221).

sam-sre: While that's running, I'm going to put a temporary routing policy to reduce new connections to eu-edge-03: set weight=0 for eu-edge-03 in the smart-routing table for 10m. That should drain existing conns and limit customer exposure.

anna-support: Notifying customer-jess: "We're investigating root cause; we found a mis-deployed cert bundle on one EU edge node and are applying a hotfix + temporary routing change. I'll message you again in ~15m." :pray:

ci-bot: deploy/cert-rot-eu03-2026-03-14-2221 succeeded :white_check_mark: (job-id: cert-rot-eu03-2026-03-14-2221)

maria-ops: Re-run openssl s_client against the IP — the intermediate is now present and chain validates. Also health checks show handshake latency back to baseline. Rolling routing weight back to normal in 5m.

sam-sre: Routing weights restored. Observability: 502 rate in eu-west-1 dropped from 2.8% -> 0.1% over the next 6m. Customer error reports reduced as well.

customer-jess: Confirming — errors dropped to near-zero, thanks. We saw a couple of retries but overall good now.

rohit-platform: Root cause write-up: race in cert-rotation parallel job where env propagation omitted intermediate bundle for a single hostgroup. Action items: (A) add a pre-check that `openssl verify` against installed chain post-rotation, failing the job if chain incomplete; (B) improve our rotation job to run with stricter env sealing to prevent empty variables; (C) add a short-window canary where we test TLS handshake from multiple public resolvers before marking job success.

devon-runtime: I'll own the `openssl verify` pre-check and can add a simple curl from 3 public resolvers (1x Google, 1x Cloudflare, 1x ISP-run) into the job script.

maria-ops: SRE follow-ups: add alert for anomalous increase in handshake timeouts per-edge-node (today this would have triggered earlier). Also add dashboard to correlate recent cert-rot jobs with handshake timeouts.

anna-support: I've updated the support ticket and included the mitigation steps and root cause. Marking the ticket as resolved pending customer confirmation.

customer-jess: All good from our side. Will reopen if anything reappears. Thanks for the fast turnaround! :raised_hands:"
